title: Vigil attendees say racism played part in death
article: The Saskatchewan Coalition Against Racism (SCAR) held a vigil on Osler Street for friends and family of Vernon Dale Crowe who died Tuesday.
Crowe experienced an apparent epileptic seizure at Soul's Harbour Mission. After becoming combative with EMS, Crowe was pepper- sprayed by a police officer in the back of the ambulance.
He was pronounced dead when the ambulance arrived at the hospital.
Police would say only that the autopsy had been completed on Wednesday, and the matter is still under investigation by the major crimes unit.
The crowd demanded answers and called for the officer who used the pepper spray to be suspended without pay. Many cried and hugged, tearfully comforting one another.
Members of Regina's inner-city community said racism and lack of patience and sensitivity on the part of police and EMS played a part in Crowe's death.

"I think the vigil a wonderful way for people to unite to speak out against police brutality and racism," said Alex Young, a volunteer for the Street Worker's Advocacy Project. "Police and EMS really do need to handle minority groups much more sensitively than they have been."
